<div class="post-content">
<p>Adobe agreed to acquire Semrush for <strong>$1.9B</strong> — paying above market comps (<strong>3.8x NTM Rev vs 3.5x</strong>) for a company whose growth rate had been declining for years. How does a SaaS business get acquired at a premium <em>despite</em> decelerating growth? By transforming its operating model: structuring pricing and packaging for expansion, building a cross-sell and up-sell motion that grows ARR per customer by cohort, and letting gross margin and free cash flow follow. This is the Semrush playbook, reconstructed from SEC filings.</p>

<p>Follow Semrush's transformation playbook:</p>
<ol>
  <li>Structure pricing and packaging to enable smooth expansion sales.</li>
  <li>Build a cross-sell and up-sell motion to grow ARR per customer by cohort.</li>
  <li>As ARR per customer rises, gross margin follows. Establish Sales & Marketing efficiency, FCF follows too.</li>
</ol>

<p>It worked for Semrush. Adobe paid above market comps (<strong>3.8x NTM Rev vs 3.5x</strong>) for <strong>$1.9B</strong>. See the valuation section below for multiple comparisons.</p>

<h2>From a Covid IPO, through a War Time Extraction, to an Efficient, Sales-Led Growth Company</h2>

<p>Despite declining growth rates, Semrush improved its operating model while scaling. Founded in St. Petersburg by <strong>Oleg Shchegolev</strong>, the company extracted 680 employees from Russia during the 2022 invasion — a decision that cost $15M and compressed FCF from $21M to $5M, but demonstrated the founder's loyalty to his team. The sales team doubled ARR per customer while new CFO <strong>Brian Mulroy</strong> (2023) compressed the cost structure. Gross margin expanded 700bps (77% → 84%, FY2024 peak), Sales & Marketing (S&M) as a % of revenue decreased by 12 points (49% → 37%), and FCF recovered from $5M to $58M by FY2025.</p>

<h2>From Self-Serve PLG to Multi-threaded RevOps</h2>

<p>The transformation spanned three years and three CROs. In late 2022, Del Humenik, the <strong>Scale-Up CRO</strong>, retired after scaling from ~$65M to $254M (2017–2022). Channing Ferrer from HubSpot, the <strong>Transformation CRO</strong>, built the Sales-Led Growth engine and transformed SalesOps to RevOps — revenue grew by $69M. Tommie O'Brien, the <strong>Execution CSO</strong> (2024), now leads the multi-threaded revenue engine from $377M to $444M. This is the kind of revenue-operations transformation we write about in <a href="/using-ai-to-enable-revops-without-breaking-your-gtm/">using AI to enable RevOps without breaking your GTM</a>.</p>

<h2>Semrush proved its ability to acquire and grow larger customers — which attracted Adobe</h2>

<p>Subscription upgrades and product cross-sells doubled ARR per customer. Acquiring enterprise customers makes the headlines. The real path to doubling ARR/customer comes from graduating bottom band customers to the middle band of $10K+ ARR customers. This requires M&A-grade ARR intelligence like upsell and cross-sell driver visibility by cohort to deploy expansion playbooks and support expansion enablement — the same discipline behind a <a href="/board-quality-arr-snowballs/">board-quality ARR Snowball</a>.</p>

<p>Adobe agreed to acquire Semrush for <strong>$1.9B</strong> — paying above market comps (<strong>3.8x NTM Rev vs 3.5x</strong>) for a company whose growth rate had been declining for years. How does a SaaS business get acquired at a premium <em>despite</em> decelerating growth? By transforming its operating model: structuring pricing and packaging for expansion, building a cross-sell and up-sell motion that grows ARR per customer by cohort, and letting gross margin and free cash flow follow. This is the Semrush playbook, reconstructed from SEC filings.</p>

<p>Follow Semrush’s transformation playbook:</p>
<ol>
  <li>Structure pricing and packaging to enable smooth expansion sales.</li>
  <li>Build a cross-sell and up-sell motion to grow ARR per customer by cohort.</li>
  <li>As ARR per customer rises, gross margin follows. Establish Sales & Marketing efficiency, FCF follows too.</li>
</ol>

<p>It worked for Semrush. Adobe paid above market comps (<strong>3.8x NTM Rev vs 3.5x</strong>) for <strong>$1.9B</strong>. See the valuation section below for multiple comparisons.</p>

<h2>From a Covid IPO, through a War Time Extraction, to an Efficient, Sales-Led Growth Company</h2>

<p>Despite declining growth rates, Semrush improved its operating model while scaling. Founded in St. Petersburg by <strong>Oleg Shchegolev</strong>, the company extracted 680 employees from Russia during the 2022 invasion — a decision that cost $15M and compressed FCF from $21M to $5M, but demonstrated the founder’s loyalty to his team. The sales team doubled ARR per customer while new CFO <strong>Brian Mulroy</strong> (2023) compressed the cost structure. Gross margin expanded 700bps (77% → 84%, FY2024 peak), Sales & Marketing (S&M) as a % of revenue decreased by 12 points (49% → 37%), and FCF recovered from $5M to $58M by FY2025.</p>
